local_facts.title: Tampa roof-work permit threshold
local_facts.claim: The City of Tampa says roof covering installation, recovering, reroofing, or repair at 500 square feet or less is exempt from a building permit; work above 500 square feet requires a permit. Its roofing guidance also says a tile roof needs a dry-in inspection before tile is installed.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A tile repair can remain narrow, but its measured area and the need to expose the underlayment determine when permitting and inspection enter the work plan.

local_facts.title: Florida’s roof-section repair line
local_facts.claim: Florida Building Code Existing Building section 706.1.1 states that no more than 25 percent of a total roof area or roof section may be repaired, replaced, or recovered within 12 months unless the entire existing roofing system or section is replaced to conform to code.
local_facts.why_it_matters: When several tile repairs are spreading across one section, the repair area must be documented before a scope is set; a tile roof cannot be treated as a series of unrelated spots.

local_facts.title: Hurricane Milton’s Tampa Bay conditions
local_facts.claim: Hurricane Milton made landfall at Siesta Key as a Category 3 hurricane on October 10, 2024. NOAA’s final report says it caused hurricane conditions from Clearwater Beach and Tampa southward, with a reported 83-knot gust at Tampa International Airport.
local_facts.why_it_matters: After severe wind and rain, a tile repair needs a wider check of surrounding tile, exposed underlayment, flashings, and roof edges—not only the piece that first looks damaged.

pricing.table_head: Tampa tile roof ranges, repair by repair

anchors.label: Residential roofing trade permit
anchors.detail: The adopted trade permit fee schedule lists a residential roofing permit at $177.00 and commercial roofing at $220.00. It took effect October 1, 2018 and carries a February 16, 2023 revision date.
anchors.source_name: City of Tampa trade permit fee schedule

anchors.label: Permit threshold and tile inspection
anchors.detail: City roofing guidance exempts roof covering work of 500 square feet or less from a building permit and requires one above that area. On tile it also requires a dry-in inspection before tile is set plus a final inspection, and points pre-March 2002 homes to hurricane mitigation retrofit requirements.
anchors.source_name: City of Tampa roofing permit requirements

anchors.label: The 25 percent roof rule and its statutory exception
anchors.detail: Section 553.844(5) provides that where 25 percent or more of a roof is repaired, replaced or recovered, only that portion must meet current code if the existing roofing system or section complied with the 2007 Florida Building Code or later. Local governments may not amend the exception.

rows.note: Matching a discontinued profile or color is what moves this from the floor to the ceiling.
